scope: Complete four-organization production segment for the missing editorial-profile cohort, with selected supported refreshes and queued identity/operating-continuity holds.

prospects.name: Coastal Defence Systems
prospects.fitSummary: Coastal Defence Systems requires ownership and operating context enrichment after the Lake Central Air Services announcement. Assess the AEROVISTA manufacturing, training and lifecycle support proposition at LOI stage, using the buyer’s Newsfile statement and official development portfolio.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: Coastal official portfolio is reachable and labels UAV platforms in development; its autonomy and performance descriptions do not provide an independent operational test record.
Lake Central buyer announcement says Coastal was acquired and the combined business will use Valkyrie; UAV production transfer and a public listing remain future intentions.
Coastal July 6 AEROVISTA release explicitly anticipates definitive agreements after an LOI; follow-up exact-name searches recovered no executed manufacturing licence.
Exact-name government-domain search for Coastal Defence Systems yielded unrelated historical coastal-defence pages, not a buyer award or product certification record.
Coastal Newsfile French-language listing returns the same July LOI announcement and no later definitive-agreement disclosure.
Lake Central homepage fetch returned HTTP 403; the buyer-authored Newsfile release remains accessible for the bounded acquisition announcement.

prospects.name: Clear Seas Research
prospects.fitSummary: Clear Seas Research lacks its editorial dossier. Its operating context now connects remote pilotage and risk assessment with Dalhousie and UQAC research, while Transport Canada and MEOPAR records clarify funded work. Assess it as a research and convening partner using clearseas.org reports and the specific contribution disclosure.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: Clear Seas about page identifies a Canadian not-for-profit research and convening mandate and publishes its Vancouver office and business contact.
Clear Seas full anchorage report recovers the 71-anchorages scope, 2016–2025 movement data and commodity/transport-system interpretation beyond the short report page.
Clear Seas MELO progress report separates completed modelling and acoustic data gathering from later validation using electric-tug and CCGS Sir John Franklin data.
Transport Canada disclosure identifies Clear Seas MELO contribution agreement 164385, CAD 150,000 and the May 2022–March 2025 agreement period; disbursement is not established.
MEOPAR names the Clear Seas SOC-I project as a 2026 seed-fund recipient and describes community co-design with Naut’sa mawt and ten Nations.
Clear Seas audited 2025 statements disclose a CAD 507,996 deficit and positive year-end net assets; the public-reporting index has no later audited year.
Clear Seas French MELO page repeats the prospective toolkit objective and UBC partnership; it adds no newer operational validation result.
Clear Seas Pilotage Technology Phase II page identifies Dalhousie and UQAC workstreams, but describes design research rather than a deployed remote-pilotage service.
Clear Seas annual-report and financial-note histories differ on incorporation/registration year; omit founded-year changes and retain the source discrepancy for review.

prospects.name: Industrial Recon
prospects.fitSummary: Industrial Recon needs a current operating-identity and ROV-service check before enriching its legacy dossier. Assess the gap between Calroc’s aerial-footage credit, the inaccessible industrialrecon.com site and the unresolved Aliter division lead.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: Industrial Recon www and apex domains failed DNS resolution in local retrieval; the web reader also failed to recover the official site. No closure is inferred.
Calroc credits Industrial Recon Commercial Drone Service for demolition-site aerial footage. The undated customer credit does not confirm today’s underwater inspection offering.
Industrial Recon public social profile describes an Aliter Technologies Canada division and ROV services; retain it as a discovery lead, not public field evidence.
Aliter official homepage fetch returned HTTP 466, and targeted official-domain searches did not recover a durable page establishing Industrial Recon division ownership.
Exact-name and parent-name public searches returned social and unrelated Recon companies; no additional durable Canadian operating-status or ROV service record was recovered.

prospects.name: SkyX
prospects.fitSummary: SkyX needs website and operating-identity recovery before a current drone dossier is credible. Compare the historical DRONE FUND drone architecture with the smart-home business now occupying skyx.com and resolve which Canadian business can be contacted.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: SkyX recorded domain now resolves to SKYX Platforms smart-home products. This conflicts with the Canadian drone-company website association; it is not evidence that the drone company closed.
DRONE FUND interview describes the drone business, SkyOne/SkyTwo, xStation and SkyVision but explicitly discusses upcoming 2020 news; no current continuity is established.
Historical Hong Kong exchange-filed reporting identifies the Canadian SkyX investment; it does not resolve the present website or 2026 operating entity.
English and French SkyX continuity searches recovered historical drone coverage, current smart-home material and unrelated namesakes, without a resolved current drone-company website.
York public-document search surfaced a SkyX story, but its document fetch returned HTTP 403; its indexed crawl date cannot establish current operating status.
